meta.title: S1 · Les 42 — Conjunctions of consequence and contrast
meta.subtitle: Lesson 42 – Conjunctions of consequence and contrast

sentences.nl: Vandaag oefenen we Nederlandse zinnen, met de grammatica van #dutchgrammar-2 les 8 en 9, over de bijzin, en voegwoorden die een consequentie uitdrukken, zoals: ‘dus’ en ‘zodat’,, en een contrast, zoals: ‘hoewel’, ‘ondanks dat’ en ‘maar’.
sentences.en: Today we practice Dutch sentences, with the grammar of #dutchgrammar-2 lessons 8 and 9, about the subordinate clause, and conjunctions that express a consequence, such as: ‘dus’ and ‘zodat’, and a contrast, such as: ‘hoewel’, ‘ondanks dat’ and ‘maar’.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Today practice we Dutch sentences, with the grammar of #dutchgrammar-2 lesson 8 and 9, about the subordinate clause, and conjunctions that a consequence express, such as: ‘so’ and ‘so that’, and a contrast, such as: ‘although’, ‘despite that’ and ‘but’.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Vandaag oefenen we" uses present tense and inverted word order because the sentence starts with a time element ("Vandaag").  
• "Met de grammatica van..." uses "met" to show accompaniment or association, similar to "with" in English.  
• "Die een consequentie uitdrukken" demonstrates the use of relative pronouns ("die") and verb-final word order in subordinate clauses.  
• Examples:  
  - "Morgen gaan we naar de markt." (Tomorrow we go to the market.)  
  - "Ik werk met de computer van mijn broer." (I work with my brother's computer.)  
  - "Zij leest een boek dat haar interesseert." (She is reading a book that interests her.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Morgen bespreken we de thema's van hoofdstuk 3, over de bijzin, en voegwoorden die een oorzaak uitdrukken, zoals: ‘omdat’ en ‘doordat’. (Tomorrow we will discuss the themes of chapter 3, about the subordinate clause, and conjunctions that express a cause, such as: ‘because’ and ‘since’.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch grammar, understanding the use of subordinate clauses and conjunctions is essential because it affects the word order of sentences. This is particularly important in both spoken and written communication, as it can alter the meaning or clarity of a sentence.

sentences.nl: En we praten over het weer.
sentences.en: And we talk about the weather.

sentences.nl: Vandaag begint de tweede week van de zomerschool,, hoewel het geen zomers weer is.
sentences.en: Today begins the second week of summer school, although it is not summer weather.

sentences.nl: Het regent erg hard.
sentences.en: It is raining very hard.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• It rains very hard.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Het regent" is the present tense of the verb "regenen" (to rain). In Dutch, weather conditions often use "het" as the subject.  
• "Erg" means "very" and is used to intensify adjectives and adverbs.  
• "Hard" is an adjective meaning "hard" or "harsh" but can also describe intensity, akin to "heavily" when describing rain.

• Extra examples:  
  - Het sneeuwt erg veel. (It snows a lot.)  
  - Het waait erg hard vandaag. (The wind is blowing very hard today.)  
  - Het is erg koud buiten. (It is very cold outside.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Het regent al de hele dag. (It has been raining all day.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, rain is a common topic of conversation due to the frequent rainy weather, and people often plan their day around the weather forecast.

sentences.nl: En het onweert zelfs.
sentences.en: And it is even thundering.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• And it thunders even.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The word "onweert" is a verb meaning "to thunder." In Dutch, weather conditions like "het onweert" use impersonal constructions with "het" (it).  
• The word "zelfs" means "even," indicating something additional or unexpected.  
• Example sentences:  
  - Het regent en het sneeuwt zelfs. (It is raining and it is even snowing.)  
  - Het is koud en het vriest zelfs. (It is cold and it is even freezing.)  
  - Het stormt en het hagelt zelfs. (It is storming and it is even hailing.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• En het bliksemt zelfs. (And it is even lightning.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, thunderstorms are relatively common, especially in the summer months. The Dutch are used to dealing with sudden weather changes, and conversations about the weather are a common small talk topic.

sentences.nl: Het bliksemt en het dondert.
sentences.en: It is lightning and thundering.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• It lightnings and it thunders.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses the impersonal verb form "het bliksemt" and "het dondert," where "het" is used as a placeholder subject, similar to "it" in English when talking about the weather.  
• The conjunction "en" simply means "and."  
• Example phrases:  
  - Het regent en het waait. (It rains and it blows [is windy].)  
  - Het sneeuwt en het vriest. (It snows and it freezes.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Het hagelt en het stormt. (It hails and it storms.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, weather is a common topic of conversation due to its unpredictability and frequent changes, making these types of sentences useful in daily small talk.

sentences.nl: De studenten zitten in de les.
sentences.en: The students are in the class.

sentences.nl: Marieke wil vandaag met de studenten naar een museum,, tenzij het nog lang blijft regenen.
sentences.en: Marieke wants to go to a museum with the students today, unless it keeps raining for a long time.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Marieke wants today with the students to a museum, unless it still long continues to rain.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Wil" is the present tense form of "willen" (to want), showing desire or intent.  
• "Tenzij" introduces a conditional clause, similar to "unless" in English.  
• "Blijft regenen" uses the verb "blijven" (to remain/continue) + infinitive, indicating an ongoing action.

Examples:  
– Hij wil morgen naar de markt, tenzij het te druk is. (He wants to go to the market tomorrow, unless it is too crowded.)  
– We blijven thuis, tenzij het weer beter wordt. (We will stay home, unless the weather improves.)  
– Ze wil met vrienden naar het concert, tenzij ze ziek is. (She wants to go to the concert with friends, unless she is sick.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Tom wil vanavond met zijn hond wandelen, tenzij het te koud is. (Tom wants to walk with his dog tonight, unless it is too cold.)

sentences.nl: Ze wil Orvelte bezoeken,, zodat de studenten iets over de geschiedenis, van Nederland leren.
sentences.en: She wants to visit Orvelte so that the students learn something about the history of the Netherlands.

sentences.nl: Orvelte is een historisch museumdorp, op 4 kilometer van het vakantiepark.
sentences.en: Orvelte is a historical museum village, 4 kilometers from the holiday park.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Orvelte is a historical museum village, at 4 kilometers from the holiday park.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Orvelte is een historisch museumdorp" is a simple sentence with the structure: [Subject] + [Verb] + [Indefinite Article] + [Adjective] + [Noun].  
• "op 4 kilometer van" uses a prepositional phrase to indicate distance, similar to how in English we use "at" or "from" to describe location or distance.

• Additional examples:  
  - "Het kasteel is op 10 kilometer van de stad." (The castle is 10 kilometers from the city.)  
  - "De school ligt op 2 kilometer van ons huis." (The school is 2 kilometers from our house.)  
  - "De bakkerij is op 500 meter van hier." (The bakery is 500 meters from here.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "De oude molen staat op 3 kilometer van het station." (The old mill is 3 kilometers from the station.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Orvelte is known as one of the most picturesque villages in the Netherlands, with preserved historical buildings and a focus on cultural heritage. It's a popular destination for tourists interested in Dutch history and rural life.

sentences.nl: Alle studenten hebben voor vandaag een fiets gehuurd,, zodat ze naar Orvelte kunnen fietsen.
sentences.en: All the students have rented a bike for today so they can cycle to Orvelte.

sentences.nl: Ze kijken naar het weerbericht op internet.
sentences.en: They are looking at the weather forecast on the internet.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• They look at the weather report on internet.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Ze" is the subject pronoun meaning "they."  
• "Kijken naar" is a verb-preposition combination meaning "to look at," where "kijken" means "to look" and "naar" means "at."  
• "Het weerbericht" is a compound noun meaning "the weather report," where "het" is the definite article "the."  
• "Op internet" means "on the internet," where "op" is a preposition meaning "on."

• Examples:  
  - "Hij kijkt naar de sterren." (He looks at the stars.)  
  - "Wij luisteren naar de radio." (We listen to the radio.)  
  - "Ze leest op haar tablet." (She reads on her tablet.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Zij zoeken naar informatie op het web. (They search for information on the web.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The sentence reflects a common practice in the Netherlands, where people frequently check the weather online due to the country's variable weather conditions.

sentences.nl: Hmmm… het wordt vandaag mooi weer,, hoewel het nu regent.
sentences.en: Hmm... the weather will be nice today, although it is raining now.

sentences.nl: Dit is toch een summer school? — Maar dit is geen zomer!
sentences.en: This is a summer school, right? — But this is not summer!

sentences.nl: Welkom in Nederland Pablo.
sentences.en: Welcome to the Netherlands, Pablo.

sentences.nl: Het is hier niet altijd mooi weer.
sentences.en: The weather is not always nice here.

sentences.nl: Ook in de zomer regent het vaak.
sentences.en: It often rains in the summer as well.

sentences.nl: Maar op de website van de summer school, schijnt de zon op alle foto’s…
sentences.en: But on the summer school's website, the sun is shining in all the photos…

sentences.nl: Haha…
sentences.en: Haha...

sentences.nl: Daarvoor moet je bij Bart zijn!
sentences.en: For that, you should go to Bart!
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• For-that must you at Bart be!

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Daarvoor" is a compound of "daar" (there) and "voor" (for), meaning "for that" or "for this purpose."  
• "Moet je" is an inversion of "je moet" (you must) due to the sentence starting with an adverbial phrase.  
• "Bij Bart zijn" indicates where you need to go or who you need to consult. "Bij" is used to indicate location or association.  

• Examples:  
  - "Daarvoor heb je een sleutel nodig." (You need a key for that.)  
  - "Bij de bakker moet je zijn voor vers brood." (You must go to the baker for fresh bread.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Daarvoor moet je naar de bibliotheek gaan!" (For that, you need to go to the library!)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, it's common to refer someone to a specific person or place for expertise or help with certain tasks, indicating a practical approach to problem-solving.

sentences.nl: Misschien wordt het straks beter.
sentences.en: Maybe it will get better soon.

sentences.nl: Na regen komt zonneschijn.
sentences.en: After rain comes sunshine.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• After rain comes sunshine.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• This sentence uses the structure "na [noun] komt [noun]" which is a common way to express sequences or consequences in Dutch.  
• The verb "komt" is in the present tense, implying a general truth.  
• The phrase is idiomatic, meaning that difficult times are often followed by better ones.

Examples:  
- Na de storm komt de rust. (After the storm comes the calm.)  
- Na een nacht komt een nieuwe dag. (After a night comes a new day.)  
- Na de winter komt de lente. (After winter comes spring.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Na hard werken komt succes. (After hard work comes success.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The phrase "Na regen komt zonneschijn" is a common Dutch proverb, similar to the English "Every cloud has a silver lining," used to encourage optimism and patience during tough times.

sentences.nl: De grote vraag is: wanneer? — Met dit weer kunnen we niet naar Orvelte.
sentences.en: The big question is: when? — With this weather, we can't go to Orvelte.

sentences.nl: Dat is te gevaarlijk vanwege de bliksem,, ondanks dat we niet zo ver moeten fietsen.
sentences.en: That is too dangerous because of the lightning, even though we don't have to cycle very far.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• That is too dangerous because of the lightning, despite that we not so far must cycle.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Dat is te gevaarlijk" uses "te" to mean "too" in the sense of excessively.  
• "vanwege de bliksem" translates to "because of the lightning," where "vanwege" is a preposition meaning "because of."  
• "ondanks dat" is a conjunction meaning "despite that." It's used to introduce a contradiction or contrast.  
• "we niet zo ver moeten fietsen" uses "moeten" (must) in the context of a mild obligation or necessity, and "niet zo ver" (not so far) limits the distance.  
• Example 1: "Dat is te duur vanwege de hoge kosten." (That is too expensive because of the high costs.)  
• Example 2: "Ondanks dat het regent, gaan we wandelen." (Despite that it is raining, we are going for a walk.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Dat is te ingewikkeld vanwege de ontbrekende informatie, ondanks dat we het proberen te begrijpen." (That is too complicated because of the missing information, despite that we are trying to understand it.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Cycling is a very common mode of transportation in the Netherlands, and weather conditions like lightning can be a serious concern for cyclists.

sentences.nl: Kunnen we niet op ‘Buienradar’ kijken? — Buienradar? — Ja, dat is een populaire website in Nederland.
sentences.en: Can't we check 'Buienradar'? — Buienradar? — Yes, that's a popular website in the Netherlands.

sentences.nl: Mijn man gebruikt het altijd.
sentences.en: My husband always uses it.

sentences.nl: Op die website zie je de regenbuien op de kaart.
sentences.en: On that website, you can see the rain showers on the map.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• On that website see you the rain showers on the map.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Op die website" (On that website) shows location and uses the preposition "op" (on).  
• "Zie je" (see you) is an example of inverted word order, common in Dutch main clauses when adverbs or prepositional phrases start the sentence.  
• "De regenbuien" (the rain showers) is the direct object of the sentence.  
• "Op de kaart" (on the map) uses "op" again, showing a location or surface.

• Extra phrases:  
  - "Op die manier leer je snel." (In that way, you learn quickly.)  
  - "In de zomer eet je veel ijsjes." (In the summer, you eat a lot of ice creams.)  
  - "Op die dag was het heel warm." (On that day, it was very warm.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "In de winkel vind je verse groenten." (In the store, you find fresh vegetables.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, checking the weather forecast, especially rain showers, is a common routine due to the country's changeable weather. Websites and apps showing rain radar are popular tools.

sentences.nl: Niet alleen op dit moment,, maar ook over een kwartier,, over een uur en over een paar uur…, zodat je precies, het weer van een specifieke lokatie weet.
sentences.en: Not only at this moment, but also in fifteen minutes, in an hour, and in a few hours..., so that you know exactly the weather of a specific location.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Not only at this moment, but also in fifteen minutes, in an hour and in a few hours..., so that you exactly, the weather of a specific location know.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses "niet alleen... maar ook..." to show contrast or addition, similar to "not only... but also..." in English.  
• "Op dit moment" translates to "at this moment," using "op" as a preposition for time.  
• The sentence structure "zodat je precies... weet" (so that you exactly... know) places the verb "weet" (know) at the end due to the subordinating conjunction "zodat."  

Examples:  
- Niet alleen zij, maar ook hij was verbaasd. (Not only she, but also he was surprised.)  
- We praten niet alleen over werk, maar ook over hobby's. (We talk not only about work, but also about hobbies.)  
- Op dit moment kunnen we niets doen. (At this moment, we can do nothing.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Niet alleen vandaag, maar ook morgen, zal het druk zijn. (Not only today, but also tomorrow, it will be busy.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Weather is a frequent topic of conversation in the Netherlands due to its variability and the impact it has on daily life, especially with activities like cycling.

sentences.nl: Goed idee Jenn.
sentences.en: Good idea Jenn.

sentences.nl: We kunnen op Buienradar kijken.
sentences.en: We can check Buienradar.

sentences.nl: Marieke gaat naar de website buienradar.nl.
sentences.en: Marieke goes to the website buienradar.nl.

sentences.nl: Kijk… wij zitten hier…
sentences.en: Look... we are sitting here...

sentences.nl: In het midden van de provincie Drenthe.
sentences.en: In the middle of the province of Drenthe.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• In the middle of the province Drenthe.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "In het midden van" translates to "in the middle of," indicating location within a specific area.  
• "Van" is a preposition meaning "of," used to show possession or relation.  
• "De provincie Drenthe" specifies the particular province, Drenthe, in the Netherlands.

• Examples:  
  - "In het midden van de stad." (In the middle of the city.)  
  - "In het midden van de nacht." (In the middle of the night.)  
  - "In het midden van de kamer." (In the middle of the room.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "In het midden van het bos." (In the middle of the forest.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
Drenthe is known for its natural landscapes and prehistoric sites like hunebedden (dolmens). It's a less urbanized province, often associated with tranquility and nature.

sentences.nl: Dit is de regenbui,, maar over een half uur is hij weg.
sentences.en: This is the rain shower, but in half an hour it will be gone.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• This is the rain shower, but in half an hour it is gone.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Dit is" means "this is," with "dit" as the demonstrative pronoun for "this."  
• "De regenbui" means "the rain shower," where "de" is the definite article for common gender nouns.  
• "Over een half uur" translates to "in half an hour," where "over" is used for time to mean "in."  
• "Hij is weg" means "it is gone," with "hij" referring to "de regenbui" and "weg" meaning "gone."

• Examples:  
  - "Dit is de krant die ik lees." (This is the newspaper that I read.)  
  - "Over een uur begint de film." (In an hour, the movie starts.)  
  - "De trein is weg." (The train is gone.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Dit is de storm, maar morgen is hij over." (This is the storm, but tomorrow it is over.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, weather changes can be quite frequent and unpredictable, so discussions about rain showers and their duration are common in daily conversation.

sentences.nl: Zie je dat? — Kortom, het wordt inderdaad mooi weer,, tenzij de voorspelling niet klopt!
sentences.en: Do you see that? — In short, the weather will indeed be nice, unless the forecast is wrong!
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• See you that? — In short, it becomes indeed nice weather, unless the forecast not correct is!

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Zie je dat?" is a question with the verb "zie" (see) coming before the subject "je" (you), which is typical in Dutch questions.  
• "Kortom" is used to summarize or conclude a point, similar to "in short" or "in summary."  
• "Het wordt" means "it becomes" or "it is going to be," using the present tense of "worden," which is often used for future meaning.  
• "Tenzij" means "unless," introducing a condition that can negate the main clause.

Extra examples:  
– "Zie jij dat boek?" (Do you see that book?)  
– "Kortom, we moeten opschieten." (In short, we have to hurry.)  
– "Het wordt morgen druk." (It will be busy tomorrow.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Zie je de regen?" (Do you see the rain?)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Weather forecasts are a common topic in Dutch conversations, as the weather can be quite changeable in the Netherlands. Discussing the forecast is a typical way to start small talk.

sentences.nl: Een tijdje later stopt het onweer, en het stopt met regenen.
sentences.en: A little while later, the storm stops, and it stops raining.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• A while later stops the thunderstorm, and it stops with raining.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Een tijdje later" means "a while later," where "een" is the indefinite article, "tijdje" is a diminutive form of "tijd" (time), and "later" means "later."  
• "Stopt" is the third person singular present tense of "stoppen," meaning "to stop."  
• "Het onweer" means "the thunderstorm," where "het" is the definite article for neuter nouns.  
• "Met regenen" uses the verb "regenen" (to rain) combined with the preposition "met" (with), indicating the action that is stopping.

• Extra Phrases:  
  - "Een uur later begint de film." (An hour later, the movie starts.)  
  - "Na het eten stop ik met werken." (After dinner, I stop working.)  
  - "Het stopt met sneeuwen in de middag." (It stops snowing in the afternoon.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Een tijdje later begint de zon te schijnen." (A while later, the sun starts to shine.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Thunderstorms in the Netherlands are common, particularly in the summer months. People often check the weather forecast to plan their outdoor activities accordingly.

sentences.nl: Zo jongens en meisjes,, tijd om onze fiets te pakken,, zodat we over een kwartiertje in Orvelte zijn.
sentences.en: So boys and girls, time to grab our bikes, so we will be in Orvelte in fifteen minutes.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• So boys and girls, time to our bicycle to grab, so that we in a quarter-hour in Orvelte are.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Zo" is used as an interjection to gather attention, similar to "So" in English.  
• "om... te" is an infinitive construction used to express purpose, similar to "to" in English.  
• "zodat" introduces a result or purpose clause, meaning "so that."  
• "over een kwartiertje" indicates a time span, translating to "in a quarter-hour."  
• Example 1: "Het is tijd om naar huis te gaan." (It's time to go home.)  
• Example 2: "We nemen de trein zodat we op tijd zijn." (We take the train so that we are on time.)  
• Example 3: "Over een uurtje komen ze aan." (They will arrive in an hour.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Zo mensen, tijd om onze spullen in te pakken zodat we voor het donker vertrekken." (So people, time to pack our things so that we leave before dark.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Orvelte is a well-preserved village in the Netherlands known for its historic buildings and is often visited as a tourist attraction. Using it in the sentence implies a casual outing or visit.

sentences.nl: En dat zien we de volgende keer bij ‘Heb je zin?’
sentences.en: And we'll see that next time on 'Are you in the mood?'

sentences.nl: Tot dan!
sentences.en: See you then!

sentences.nl: Doei!
sentences.en: Bye!

vandaag.spelling: The combination 'aa' in 'vandaag' indicates a long /aː/ sound, typical for Dutch vowels.
vandaag.fast: The final /x/ in 'vandaag' may be softened or dropped in rapid speech, especially if followed by a vowel.

oefenen.spelling: The sequence 'oe' represents a long /uː/ sound.
oefenen.fast: In casual speech, the final /n/ in ‘oefenen’ may be fully assimilated or nasalized before a vowel.

grammatica.spelling: The initial gr- and -a- in 'grammatica' follow the usual Dutch pronunciation rules for similar Greek-origin words.
grammatica.fast: In rapid speech, the final /a/ in 'grammatica' may be pronounced as a schwa [ə] when followed by a word starting with a consonant.

van.spelling: The short vowel /ɑ/ is common in monosyllabic words ending in -n.
van.fast: The final /n/ in ‘van’ is often elided in casual speech, particularly before consonants.

les.spelling: Short /ɛ/ in a closed syllable followed by a voiceless /s/.
les.fast: In rapid speech, the final /s/ in ‘les is’ may become voiceless between vowels, leading to a pronunciation like [lɛsɪs].

over.spelling: The open syllable 'o-' shows the long /oː/ vowel.
over.fast: In connected speech, final /r/ in 'over' may be pronounced as a flap or even omitted depending on regional accents.

die.spelling: In Dutch, the pronoun 'die' is pronounced with a long /i/ sound, which is common for pronouns and demonstratives.
die.fast: In connected speech, 'die' may become a reduced vowel sound, especially in fast speech or informal contexts.

een.spelling: The article ‘een’ is pronounced with a long /eː/ to distinguish it from the numeral ‘één’, which has a stressed pronunciation.
een.fast: In rapid speech, ‘een’ may be reduced to a schwa sound /ən/ when it is unstressed.

dat.spelling: Short vowel /ɑ/ in a closed syllable is represented by a single 'a'.
dat.fast: In connected speech, the /d/ in ‘dat is’ may be voiced to a soft [d̪] before the vowel.

maar.spelling: The long vowel /aː/ appears in the open syllable.
maar.fast: In fast speech, the /r/ in 'maar ik' may be reduced or assimilated to the following vowel.
